clinical_knowledge.topic: Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management follows an evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe burning pain followed by grouped vesicles on red base across forehead and tip of nose (Hutchinson sign)

Key HPI features: 64M presenting with painful unilateral dermatomal vesicular eruption along ophthalmic branch of V1 trigeminal nerve with vesicles on nasal tip (Hutchinson sign) requiring urgent Valacyclovir and ophthalmology exam for anterior uveitis.
Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Herpes simplex virus infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Vesicles on the tip or side of the nose (Hutchinson's sign) — high risk of ocular involvement and permanent vision damage.
management_principles: Start systemic antiviral therapy promptly (for example, oral valacyclovir when appropriate) and arrange urgent ophthalmology assessment for ocular involvement
Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus: severe burning pain followed by grouped vesicles on red base across forehead and tip of nose (Hutchinson sign). 64M presenting with painful unilateral dermatomal vesicular eruption along ophthalmic branch of V1 trigeminal nerve with vesicles on nasal tip (Hutchinson sign) requiring urgent Valacyclovir and ophthalmology exam for anterior uveitis.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus.
reference_soap.plan: Start systemic antiviral therapy promptly (for example, oral valacyclovir when appropriate), ideally within 72 hours of rash onset but without delaying treatment for suspected ophthalmic involvement. Arrange same-day urgent ophthalmology assessment to evaluate for keratitis, uveitis, and elevated intraocular pressure. Provide analgesia and counsel on urgent review for visual change, eye pain, or photophobia.

teaching.one_liner: Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus in the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, causing painful vesicles across the forehead — vesicles on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson's sign) predict eye involvement and need urgent ophthalmology evaluation.
red_flags: Vesicles on the tip or side of the nose (Hutchinson's sign) — high risk of ocular involvement and permanent vision damage

must_ask.say: Did the burning pain start before the blisters appeared?
Is the rash confined to one side of your forehead, and does it involve the tip of your nose?
Any eye pain, redness, or vision changes?
How many days ago did the rash appear?
Do you have any condition that weakens your immune system?
